Summary  
Data source overview:  
The paper analyses why engagement-optimised recommendation engines (Twitter push-notification case study) can harm users because engagement signals are an unreliable proxy for the latent construct “value”.  It proposes a measurement-theoretic solution: model a binary latent variable Value inside a Bayesian network, identify it with a single strong explicit-feedback “anchor” (e.g. “See Less Often”), estimate the factors with a matrix-adjustment algorithm fed by both randomised and algorithmic data, and then use P(Value=1│behaviours) as the optimisation objective.  Large-scale internal-structure tests on millions of Twitter users show the model produces plausible inferences and clearly out-performs naïve baselines.  Interventions extracted include (i) deploying value-probability as the live ranking objective, (ii) designing richer explicit feedback channels to serve as anchors, and (iii) routinely re-estimating the latent-value model to cope with behavioural drift.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[86]  
The fabric covers every reasoning step—risk → proxy-gap problem → anchor-LVM theory → measurement design → concrete estimation mechanisms → empirical validations → actionable interventions.  All nodes inter-connect, comply with naming granularity, and JSON fields/edges match spec.  Possible prompt improvements: explicitly remind extractor that many sections have repeated names (“Identification …”) so using the exact subsection header closest to the relevant sentence avoids ambiguity when filling node/edge rationales.

Inference strategy justification  
Only light inference (confidence 2) was used to map the text’s suggested maintenance and UI design practices into explicit AI-safety interventions.  All other nodes/edges are based on direct statements or quantitative results (confidence ≥3).

Extraction completeness explanation  
14 nodes (~1.4 × 10-4 of source length) reflect every distinct construct appearing along the causal-interventional chain; no concept in the core reasoning loop was omitted, and every intervention is supported by at least one validation evidence node.

Key limitations  
• The source does not yet report user-well-being field trials, so risk-level mitigation evidence remains indirect.  
• Edge confidences are estimated qualitatively because p-values were not provided.  
• The implementation mechanism node was split into two sub-mechanisms (estimation algorithm and anchor choice); further decomposition (e.g. into specific matrices) might help future merging but would exceed required granularity.
